Entities, correct and otherwise

A correct one first, so the fixture is not uniformly broken: Eastfield & Lowry Dock reported <40 minutes, which is "good" by the standard in use.

An ampersand that is never an entity at all: Marchwood & Brantham, written the way somebody types it rather than the way it should be escaped.

A numeric reference with no digits in it: &#; and a second one with nonsense where the digits belong: &#zz; neither of which resolves to anything.

A named reference that does not exist: ¬arealentity; sitting mid-sentence, and a bare ampersand at the end of a line &

A stray semicolon with no entity in front of it; and an escaped one &; doubled up.

The last paragraph is ordinary, so the document ends with a region that contains no entity problems at all and can be edited normally.
